string.text: Good day, Lieutenant, sir.
Thirty-five percent... Hey, Doc, think they'll cut us too? Honestly, I'd haul ass outta here without a second thought.
Go ahead, Lieutenant.
I'm listening, Rogovets.
What do you want?
Well, look at that. A living soul.
What do you want, soldier?
Greetings, brother.
Freeze! Not one more step!
Hold still. A pseudodog's gonna cut you way before they do if you keep daydreaming on patrol.

There was no dog out there, LT, I'm telling you... It was... fuck knows what it was. Something grey, between the trees. I look, it's standing there. I blink, it's gone. And then something cracked to my left...
Something grey, you say...
Yeah! My buddy swears it's just hallucinations from no sleep. But here's what I think: I haven't slept right since basic, and I've never seen anything like that.
Did you report it to the colonel?

Hell yeah, I did! And that bastard wrote me up for it, said I go out on patrol drunk. I haven't touched a bottle in a month, for the record! How the hell did he even get promoted, huh? I just wanna get out of this hole already...
I see. Are you in pain?
Yeah, but it's nothing...
You stay in bed till the end of the week. Come see me in 3 days, I'll give you more painkillers. No patrols, don't strain that arm. Got it?
Got it, Doc, thank you. Maybe I'll play some cards with the guys... How about you, wanna join us?
No, thanks, I'm busy today. Take care, soldier.
Lieutenant Rogovets reporting, Colonel.
At ease, Lieutenant. How's that patrolman's wound? Nothing serious, I hope?
No, sir. I gave him first aid and painkillers, he'll live, but...
When can he return to duty? Today? Tomorrow?
Um... Well, he needs to rest at least until the end of the week, physical strain could...
But he can at least stand guard? Just stand by the sandbags?

Without a rifle, maybe. If he holds a pistol in his left hand, I think he could manage. Though then I'd have to prescribe him more meds, morphine and so on... which, by the way, we're running out of. I sent you a request about medical supplies a week ago...

Supplies... There won't be any supplies, Lieutenant. They're cutting everything: vehicles, people, provisions. Remember the last time they brought us consumables? 2 months ago. And the last time they sent reinforcements to this base? Six months ago. Ever since this crisis started back on the Big Land, our troubles started too. Only I think we're in an even deeper shit than those guys in their offices. And you know what... Those headquarters assholes used to nag us every single day: asking for the impossible, always demanding some kind of "results". And now they've just gone quiet. Once a month a radiogram comes in, with a list of supplies or people to cut, and that's it... Like nobody needs us here anymore, you understand?
I understand...
So, why did I even call you here... Son of a bitch, my head's been splitting for weeks now, I can't think straight about anything...
Have you been taking my pills?

To hell with your pills, they're useless! Fine, back to business. I'll keep it short: we're not completely fucked yet, but we will be very soon if we do nothing. As you may have noticed yourself, the number of people at this base goes down every day. On top of the regular losses in skirmishes with mutants and people, now our soldiers are going missing. They can just up and leave their post at any moment, for no reason at all! And sometimes whole checkpoints stop answering my calls. I don't even send squads to check anymore, there's a chance they won't report back either. Cases of nervous breakdowns in the garrison are on the rise too, but you must know that already, being the medic.

Long story short, we have a critical shortage of personnel. So I have to take extreme measures. Rogovets, I know you have a lot of experience behind you: you took part in Operation Fairway, you were in Pripyat, and even after getting hit by the strongest psy-emission, you made it out alive. We critically need your experience if we want to survive. So here are your orders: as of today, you're not just medical service, I'm transferring you to the infantry. You'll carry out combat missions as part of other assault teams. I need every gun I can get, and on top of that, you've got a head that's been through Pripyat.
Commander, sir, I've never even...

You'll keep your medic duties, nothing to be done about that, we don't have any other experienced doctors here. We'll cut your routine rounds down to once a day instead of twice, and the rest of the time you're on duty. Is that clear?
Colonel, sir...

You'll get your gear from the quartermaster, he's sitting in the warehouse counting the ammo for the 20th time. Once you've got your gear, report to your post, and I'll contact you later about your first assignment.

Colonel, sir! I'm not fit for this at all! That's exactly why I'm a medic, because I'm a lousy shot, and-and just in general! In Pripyat, because of me... the whole team almost died, I... I'll just be a burden to the men. I'd better stay at the base, make medicine here... It'll be easier for the guys if I stay at the base instead of getting in their way.

Now you listen to me, Lieutenant. I know this isn't easy, but it's hard on all of us right now. I know your Pripyat story, I read Degtyarev's reports. And your experience is exactly what we need. Something is going on here... something nobody understands. Constant headaches, for me and the other men, a lot of them hear some kind of screams and see strange lights coming from the swamps, and some soldiers just dissolve into the fog, leaving all their belongings and weapons behind... I don't know what it is, and I don't want to know. But you've seen... things like that in Pripyat. So you'll take a look. Do you understand now?
I... I understand, Colonel.

And about the other men, you can walk around the base, ask them what they think about all this devilry. Every one of them will tell you how hard and rough it is here. No, I'm serious, talk to the men. As far as I know, you were a bit detached from reality even before Pripyat, and now you've completely shut yourself in, after that psy-strike. Talking will do you good... Alright, we've chatted long enough. Carry on with your orders!
Yes, sir!
Permission to speak, Colonel?
Granted.
What's even going on back on the Big Land? The radio just mumbles the same thing over and over, nobody can make sense of it.

The radio won't tell you the truth. But I'll tell you what I see on paper and in practice. In six months, 3 of our generals "retired for health reasons". Healthy men, I knew two of them personally, they were some of the few honest officers left. The Deputy Minister of Defense, same story. Somebody is methodically taking out the people who were responsible for the Zone... and their seats are taken by people who don't need us here. The cuts aren't about saving money, Lieutenant. Somebody is clearing out the Zone. For what, don't ask me, I don't know.
And what happened to the other bases? We weren't the only one.

That's just it, there were others. The Cordon checkpoint was shut down this winter, they called it "optimization". Yeah, they took the most effective checkpoint of them all and "optimized" it. Bullshit... The base in the Dark Valley, at the factory: the whole garrison abandoned their positions, left the vehicles behind, and nobody ever made contact again... Familiar symptoms, huh?.. The outpost near Yantar, by the scientists' mobile bunker, after that... incident... no, I don't even want to remember it. The rest of the checkpoints and outposts in the Zone, a similar story. Cut, fallen in battle, gone missing. We're the last major base of the Armed Forces in the Zone. On paper there are five of us left, but in reality it's just me, talking to the void on the radio.
Colonel, sir, have you ever... thought about leaving yourself?

I have... Back in '11, at the Cordon, when I was still doing field assignments, I thought: I'll serve my time and then leave. I served my way up to colonel. And you know what I realized? There's nowhere to go. On the Big Land I'm just a crazy soldier from the Chernobyl hole that nobody wants to listen to. Here at least somebody needs me... That's enough, Lieutenant, drop it.
No more questions.
Then don't just stand there, soldier, get to work!
Good day. I'm here for my gear.
Wha?! Ah, it's you, Rogovets. What the hell do you need gear for? You know we've got a total ammo shortage? And a people shortage too.
I can help with the second one, that's why I'm here. Didn't the colonel tell you?
Tell me what? Ah, shit, right, they put you in the infantry. Sorry, I forgot. So much going on... you forget your own name in this hole. Alright, hang on, let's find you something...
Is the gear situation that bad?
Bingo. If only it were that simple, Lieutenant... Alright, here, take it. Not much, but it'll do for you. You've already got armor, which is good, 'cause I've got nothing but torn rags.
Thanks anyway, see you...
Hey, where are you going? I'm not done yet. Did the colonel give you an assignment?
Well, he's supposed to contact me, why?
Ah, I see, go then. Later, when you're done, drop by, there's a problem I need to sort out, your help would come in handy. That's it, go on, get outta here.
Got a minute?
One minute, yeah. Two, no.
What do you think is going on at this base? Off the record.

Off the record? It's a fucking mess, Doc, only it's a sneaky one, slippery as hell. A regular mess is when people shoot, when creatures crawl out of every crack, when your convoy gets sent into an anomaly field... But here it's quiet. People evaporate and leave all their stuff behind: armor, gun, letters, money. MONEY, you get it?! Where does a man go without his money and his gun? And the most interesting part: the rats. For six months they chewed through my warehouse, and now I haven't seen a single one in a month. Rats are the first to know when the ship's going down. Draw your own conclusions.
Where did you even get your contacts in the Zone?

Heh, I've lived long, traded a lot, and kept my nose out of other people's business. How do you think garrisons in the Zone get their supplies when the General Staff forgets about them? Through contacts like these. Half the "army" warehouses in the Zone go through the same hands as the stalkers' loot, and not for the first year. I'll tell you more: we had channels with Duty too, back when there was a Duty. Ammo for canned food, canned food for artifacts, artifacts to the Big Land... That's it, forget what you heard. Inventory time.
Have you been serving here long?

A year here, but I've been stuck in the Zone itself for 5 years now. I've outlasted three bases already: everybody got rotated out, and I always stayed. And you know why? I've got nobody on the Big Land, but here I've got a warehouse. Here I'm needed, without me they'd strip the place clean in a week. Or you dumbasses would run out of ammo, and who'd get you supplies under the table then? Who'd sign you out new gear when you come back with a gun beat to hell again? A fool, huh? Hah, I remember my little brother, a machine gunner, he used to tell me that all the time, kept telling me to drop it all, quit and go back to the Big Land... Alright, go, Doc, your minute's up.
Alright, I'll go.
See you. And close the door, there's a draft.
Lieutenant Rogovets, report to HQ immediately for new orders. Colonel Kuznetsov.
Rogovets, your first assignment: go down into the tunnels under our base. Check on the garrison there and help them if needed.
Private of the Agroprom Research Institute garrison. Wounded on patrol, relieved of duty until the end of the week.
Commander of the last major Armed Forces base in the Zone. Has served here since 2011.
Head of the warehouse. Five years in the Zone, outlived three bases. Knows everyone who brings anything at all out here.
Good day. They sent me from the base...
Well, obviously not from Mars! Who are you?
Lieutenant Rogovets, field medic.
Hm, don't remember you. Well, I don't visit the infirmary much, that's probably why. What are you here for?
The colonel sent me to check on your condition and find out if you need any help.
Help? Tell him to give us more ammo and some grub! Fuck, once every 2 weeks they toss a crate down the stairs, not even a "hello", and we're starving down here, for the record!
It's like that for everyone right now, not just you.

And I don't give a shit about "everyone", got it? All I care about is my men, who eat one loaf of bread for the whole day. And you can't go upstairs and ask, they write you up right away for leaving your post. Fuckin' bastards.
Eh, alright, man, sorry I yelled at you. My nerves are shot in this hole. You wanted to check on the guys?
Yes. The colonel also ordered me to help you with your urgent problems, but I'm kind of...

We've got problems up to our necks, the old man shouldn't worry too much... So, about the guys: you can go around to each of them here and ask how everyone's feeling, and then decide how to help them and what meds to prescribe. And about the problems... Recently some creature attacked a patrol and dragged one of our guys into the northern part of the underground. I sent the guys to get him back, but in the end they burned through a ton of ammo and came back empty-handed. Now the men are too scared shitless to go there. Their excuse is that there's more than one mutant down there. Bullshit, if you ask me. So I'm giving this job to you: show these crybabies how to deal with the Zone's filth. Put a bullet in the head of the thing that killed our comrade, and report back to me.
I'm... not sure I'm right for this job, Sergeant. The last time I fired a gun was back in Pripyat, and even then blindly, without really aiming...

Oh, so you were in Pripyat too?! From Fairway or something? Then this'll be a piece of cake for you! I sent a mark to your PDA where the missing soldier's signal was last seen, the mutant's sitting somewhere around there. Oh, and one more thing: the men keep complaining to me about their problems, and I can't help them, for obvious reasons. Since you came down here anyway, ask the guys what they need. And I'll give you something as a reward, deal?
Eh... Deal. See you, Sergeant.
Goddammit, I'm never going in there again!
You alright, Lieutenant? We heard shots and screams...

Because your men were right, there's more than one mutant there! Two bloodsuckers attacked me. One of them was wounded, sitting by the body, I finished it off quick. But the second one jumped out when I'd already relaxed and started examining your soldier. It's a miracle it didn't kill me...

Well, it all worked out in the end, huh? Here, take a pack of armor-piercing rounds, don't be too down. I'll send the guys for the body, no need for him to rot there, at least we'll bury him like a human being. Thanks for the help.
*mumbles something unintelligible in reply*
Wait, Sergeant. I think I've already met that thing...
So that was you making all that noise?! We heard shots and screams, thought we'd lost another one... You alright, Lieutenant?

Well, look at you, Doc! Here, take a pack of armor-piercing rounds, you earned it. I'll send the guys for the body, at least we'll bury him like a human being. And since you're here: the men keep complaining to me about their problems, and I can't help them. Ask the guys what they need, and I'll give you something as a reward, deal?
Sergeant, a couple of questions, if you don't mind.
I never mind, I've got nobody down here to talk to except the rats. Ask away.
How long have you been down here?

God knows what month it is. They promised rotation in six weeks. Yeah, right. After that I stopped counting days, what's the point? My guys have forgotten what daylight looks like, half of them have an eye twitch from this darkness. Two of them already sleep with a flashlight on, they can't do it otherwise. Just burns through the batteries. I sent a request upstairs: "hold on, no reserves". So we're holding on. By our teeth now, brother, but we're holding on.
What even lives in this underground?

It used to be rats and a couple of bloodsuckers, we knew every one of them like the neighbors in our building. But this last month... new sounds showed up. Not mutant sounds. I've learned mutants over all this time like the alphabet: what scrapes where, who breathes where. Something else. Either water singing somewhere, or... Look, you're the doctor here. Tell me honestly: can a whole squad lose their minds at once? The same way? All hearing the same thing at the same time?
It can happen. Usually psy-emission is to blame. Maybe a controller has moved in?

Maybe... Or maybe we really are hearing something? They gave all of us psy-blockers back when a controller lived here, before some stalker took it down. We thought a new one would come. We drank that crap, doesn't help for shit, and those sounds just got louder.
Why don't you go down to the lower levels?

Because I lost 4 men down there, and I'm not planning to lose any more. Something weird has settled in down there, soldier. There were no screams, no shooting, nothing at all. Just silence. How the fuck do 4 well-armed men just up and vanish without a sound?
You just haven't been to the surface in a while if you're asking that...
Do you know where the way down to the lower levels is?

I know, but you won't get there. Not because I said so. That way down just doesn't exist anymore. After a group of our men went missing down there, I ordered that passage blown up, so nothing could crawl out of it. I don't know about other routes down. Word is, the local diggers might know secret ways into that hell... But my advice to you, as one serviceman to another: don't go there. The colonel has already lost several groups in those tunnels, and he tried to send ours too. There's evil sitting down there, waiting for something... But what?
That's all, thanks.
Take care, Doc. Drop by if it gets too depressing up there.
Hello, soldier, need any help?

Well, actually, there is one thing. See, me and the guys went out on patrol, and mutants attacked us... Well, you probably know already. Some invisible thing dragged one of us off somewhere, the rest ran for it, and I ran after them. Man, I was so ashamed of myself after... It was just pure animal fear, and a voice in my head screamed that I had to run. Never had anything like that before... And when I came to my senses, I realized I'd dropped my award pistol. It means a lot to me, I've been carrying that gun for so many years... I'm too scared to go back there, and the guys will tell me to piss off if I ask them, so could you find that pistol and bring it back to me? I think it's somewhere in the tunnel north of here, some anomalies have popped up there recently, I can't say more precisely.
In an anomaly field, you say... Alright, wait here, I'll try to get it.
Here's your pistol.

Thank you so much, brother! I don't even know how to thank you... Oh, I know, here, take some grenades. Blowing them up down here is a lost cause anyway, God forbid we bury ourselves alive in these tunnels... Good luck, brother!
Hey there, need any help?

Hm... There is something. It's nothing urgent, more like my curiosity acting up... A while ago I was on watch while everybody was sleeping, and I heard strange sounds from the northern part of the underground: long, drawn-out wailing, like somebody was singing church hymns. And then screams and gunshots. Scared the hell out of me, I couldn't sleep the whole next day. I'm telling you, it wasn't mutants, no mutant "sings" like that. Go check it out, would you? And I'll slip you something not exactly legal for us servicemen in return, deal?
*tenses up* You know, after what you just said, I don't really feel like going there. Though I don't have much else to do... Show me where to go.
This place of yours... is like a train station.
What happened down there?
I found 2 bodies: some digger, and a stalker from some unknown faction. Creepy suit he had on... On him I found a PDA with these audio recordings, here, listen.
*listens* Brrr, what a voice. I wonder what he could've been looking for down there?... Find anything else?

Yes, on the digger I found part of some area maps, they show some regions of the Zone's South. That's probably what this... someone was after. Oh, and then his "battle brothers" attacked me, I had to kill them.

Oh, now that's interesting! Hand over the maps, I'll pass them on to command, this should interest the colonel. And you've got a reward coming. Sooo, let me just... Here, look! Picked it up by the electros yesterday. Just shh, don't show it around too much. We don't exactly love artifacts in the army. Slip it in your pocket quietly and go on your way.
And... what makes you think I won't report this to the higher-ups?
Because I know that after just 10 minutes of wearing this trinket, you won't want to part with it. That's it, don't hang around here too much. My respects.
Soldier of the Agroprom Research Institute underground garrison.
Private Vulfov
Private Teslya
Sergeant Slobodenyuk
Head of the underground garrison. Has been stuck down there for months, no rotation.
Soldier's corpse
Digger's corpse
A digger stalker. Died fighting back.
Unknown stalker
An unfamiliar suit model. Faction cannot be identified.
Unknown stalker's PDA

A battered PDA taken from a body. Its memory holds a single audio recording: "This is the end... I'm not long for this world... But I've fulfilled my mission: I caught up with the stalker who stole part of the maps right from under our noses... I finished him off. Their whole group... finished off. But... I got hurt myself... I can feel the light of my soul fading. A pity... that I'll never see the Liberation of the Zone... My battle brothers, if you hear this... then tell... tell Fulgrim that I did it..."
Old Exclusion Zone maps
Old maps of some regions of the Exclusion Zone. Looks like the digger got them from some lab or underground. There are blood stains on some of the pages.
How are you feeling, soldier? Any complaints?
Here.
Good to hear. Take care.
I don't have any right now. I'll bring some when I find them.
Thanks a lot, Doc. At least somebody here cares about people. Here, take this, I've got some extra.
Take care, Lieutenant. Oh, wait, here, it's just lying around anyway.
Still alive, I guess. Just ripped my back open on some rebar climbing down from the tower. A couple of bandages would be nice, it's already stuck to my jacket.
Cut my hand hauling crates. No big deal, but it keeps bleeding. Got a bandage?
My knee. Can't bend it properly for the second day now, and I'm due on watch. Got a medkit?
Got hit by shrapnel when somebody popped a grenade in the tunnel. Two medkits would be great, Doc. I'm not greedy, I just have a lot of holes.
LT, I haven't slept for two days, I'm shaking all over, and something's pressing in my side. I need an army one, the regular ones don't do anything.
Think I caught a dose on my rounds yesterday. The dosimeter was clicking like crazy, and I didn't notice right away. Some anti-rad would help.
I'm healthy, Doc. I just haven't slept a wink for I don't know how many nights. It's not medicine I need here... you get me. Got anything?
Healthy as a horse, Doc. Except my ears are ringing from all this silence. Better check on those guys over there, they're walking around grey in the face.
Oh-ho, it's been a while since anyone from the surface came down here. Come on over, brother, let's talk.
Maybe so. Any more questions?
Mission accomplished, Colonel.
Aha, excellent. Any trouble with the "underground" guys?
There were some, but we...

Well, that's great. Now listen up, I've got a new assignment for you. A boring one this time: go down to our quartermaster, take 3 crates of supplies from him and deliver them to our checkpoints. We barely have any supplies, of course, but our men need them desperately right now. I know it's dangerous going alone, but we have no other choice, I can't send more people with you. If you sense anything strange, run straight back to the base.
Understood, I'll be going then...

Hold on, I'm not done... *lowers his voice* Also take a special case from the quartermaster, tell him it's on my orders. After you finish the job, don't come back to the base, head straight to the stalker camp. Talk to their leader there, Seriy, and give him this case, he won't ask any unnecessary questions.
Hm, alright. And what's in this case?
That's none of your business. The less you know, the better you sleep. *raises his voice* Are your orders clear, Lieutenant? Then move out, I'll contact you when you're done.
Yes, sir!
Hello again, I'm here for the checkpoint supplies.
Uh-huh, the old man told me already. Yeah, what a shitshow, at this rate we'll be jumping on the enemy with knives, the ammo shortage is at 70%. Here, take it and get outta here...
Thanks, but there's one more thing... A personal request from the colonel, he said you'd understand...

What?! I don't get it, what request? Hold on, let me remember... Hmmm... Ah, that's probably what he meant. Fuck, couldn't he just say what he needs? Like I'm supposed to remember who's got what personal request, ugh.
And what's in this container? The colonel said it's for...

How should I know? Kuznetsov told me not to look inside, so I didn't, I've got enough on my plate. And I don't recommend you do either, unless you want your ass handed to you. By the way, you reminded me of something, good thing you dropped by. Remember I told you about a job, before you went down to the underground?
Yeah, what job?

Ahem... I don't know if I'm talking to the right person, but... Well, since I've started... I've mentioned a hundred times that we're screwed on ammo, and I don't like sitting on my hands and watching us die with empty mags. So I decided to take the situation into my own hands, since command doesn't give a damn about us. I reached out to some of my contacts in the Zone, and I managed to arrange an ammo supply for our garrison. And today the first deal with the suppliers is supposed to happen. They're supposed to haul in a big batch of ammo, and if all goes well, there'll only be more deliveries in the future.
Hm, that... actually sounds pretty good! What's the catch, Sergeant?
The catch is, I made the deal with bandits.
Uh, what?!

Keep it down! So listen here: there won't be any deal. I can't stand that criminal scum, and I'm not going to do any business with them. I told them we'd bring 25 grand in cash and make the exchange today. But it's all much simpler: the only thing waiting for them here will be lead. And that's where I need your help...

Wait, wait, this is way the hell outside regulations! Have you completely lost your mind, making deals with bandits? And what makes you think I won't tell Kuznetsov about this? Why did you ask me for help, of all people?

Because you were in the underground and saw with your own eyes how the guys live down there: a loaf a day and half a mag per man. You're a doctor, you know what happens when people have nothing to eat and nothing to shoot back with. And you won't go snitching, I can read people like a book. Our garrison is in a situation where we can't be too picky about who we deal with and who we don't. Whether it's by the regulations or not doesn't bother me much. What bothers me is that tomorrow, if a wave of mutants comes at us, we'll have nothing to shoot with. So I'm solving the problem however I can. Any more questions?

Because I noticed an interesting trinket on your belt. You should hide your artifact better, it sticks out too much. And if you're carrying around not-quite-legal stuff, then you understand yourself that we have to use every advantage, even a small one, to survive. And our garrison is in a situation where we can't be too picky about who we deal with and who we don't. Whether it's by the regulations or not doesn't bother me much. What bothers me is that tomorrow, if a wave of mutants comes at us, we'll have nothing to shoot with. So I'm solving the problem however I can. Any more questions?
No, sir...

Then here's your task: in a few hours the bandits are supposed to show up at the meeting point, I'll contact you when they're there. Your job is simple: kill them, take the ammo and come back to me. As a reward I can throw you a scope, deal?
Deal. Is that all?
Yeah, that's all, you can go. Wait for my signal.
I've got bad news...
Why's that all of a sudden? Where are the ammo crates?
They didn't have any crates. What's more, they set up an ambush for me themselves. They never planned any exchange, they came to kill right away.
Damn them! I knew nothing good would come from them...
Then why'd you go for the exchange? Tried to scam bandits, hah..

Hey, don't you get smart with me! Though you're right, of course, it's my own fault. At least they didn't get you too bad. Alright, whichever way you look at it, we didn't lose anything, and we made the Zone a little bit cleaner, so you did earn your reward. I promised you a scope, right? Lemme see what I've got...
Here, pick one: the 1P78 "Kashtan" with 3x magnification, for long range, or the OKP-7 with no magnification, good for close-range firefights.
The 1P78 "Kashtan".
The OKP-7.

Alright, take it. Even though our plan didn't work out, I'm still grateful you agreed to help. So, now I have to do inventory all over again... Huh, why are you standing there? Off you go, Lieutenant, don't get in my way.
Hello, soldier. I brought you supplies from command.
Good day, Lieutenant, sir. Finally, somebody bothered to do it. Oh, I know you, you're the medic from the main base!
Yeah, that's me. Glad I could help, I'll be moving on...

Wait! The last time we were at the infirmary was several months ago, and we get all kinds of injuries almost every day. Don't leave your fellow soldiers in trouble: check my men for wounds and give them meds if you have any.
Hm... Alright, but only if it's quick, I still need to stop by the other posts.

I promise it won't take long. And to make it more fun for you, here, take this, a TOZ-34 over-under. We took it from some stalker, he looked way too suspicious to us. It'd just be gathering dust in the warehouse, now it'll serve you instead.
Nothing serious, LT, ripped my hand on the barbed wire while we were patching the passage. Just need a bandage.
Took a tumble off the tower the day before yesterday, scraped up my whole shoulder. Bandaged it myself, but it's already festering. A couple of fresh bandages would help.
It's this cough, Doc. Third week now. During the day it's bearable, but at night nobody can sleep because of me. A medkit would help, there's gotta be something in there for this.
Last week I chased a dog down into the lowland, and the counter was clicking like crazy down there. I've been nauseous ever since. Got any anti-rad?
Got my finger pinched by a rifle stock, the nail came off. Funny, I know, but it's hard to shoot. Wrap it up, will you?
My side hurts, Doc. Not sharp, just a dull pain, all the time. Maybe I bruised it when I fell into a trench. Got a medkit?
Good day, need some ammo? The colonel's feeling generous today.
Oh, thanks, brother, we've been waiting for you for a long time. Now, how can I thank you...
I don't need anything, trust me...
Come on, we don't mind. Here, take a couple of VOGs, none of us has a grenade launcher anyway, maybe at least you'll get one.
Thanks anyway... Wait, what's that noise?
Hello, Lieutenant Rogovets here, delivering your ammo.
Yeah, yeah, hand it over... Shit, why the hell did they give us 5.45s? All our guns take 7.62, don't they know that? Ah, screw it, you can keep them, we don't need 'em for shit anyway.
Thanks.
Hey. What are you doing sitting here alone? The camp's a stone's throw away, it'll be safer there than out here.
Greetings, serviceman. Well... I'm resting. The camp is noisy. People are always dividing something: loot, canned food, their fears. But here it's quiet. You can hear...
Hear... what?
The Zone... You're on business, I can see. Going to Seriy, I bet. Seriy's a good man, only tired. You're all tired here... A hard day for you today, Lieutenant?
How do you know I'm a lieutenant?
Your bearing. And the way you walk... like a man many owe their lives to, while he himself owes nothing to anyone. A medic, are you?
Good guess.

Well, well. Patching people up is a good thing. Only here's what I've learned in the Zone, serviceman: patching people up is like painting this booth. The boards are rotten. Sometimes, to save something, you don't patch it, you replace it. Entirely.
...A philosopher, I see. Alright, take care. Don't sit here too long, it's a restless place.
Restless, yes... It's nothing. Everything in the Zone has one chance to change, Lieutenant. Places and people alike... Go on, they're waiting for you.
Greetings, stalker.
Well, hello there, soldier boy. Don't see your kind around here often. You here on business, or what?
On business. You're Seriy, right? I've got something for you... *lowers his voice* from the colonel.

Hm, from Kuznetsov? Alright, spit it out, what does that old geezer want from me? I still remember him squeezing money out of me at the Cordon for passing under the bridge. That nagging "five hundred, pay up" of his still rings in my ears...
This time he's giving you money. Or something better, I'm not sure myself. Anyway, he asked me to give you this case, said you'd understand without words.

Well, well! You've got me curious. Alright, hand it over, let's see what we've got here... So... Aha... Uh-huh... I get it. Alright, soldier, you've done your job, you're free to go. And if you're interested in some small side jobs, I can offer you a couple, or ask the guys around the camp.
I've got a couple of questions for you.
Well, I'm a lousy talker, but I'll do my best to answer. What do you want to know?
Tell me, what's new in the Zone lately?

New? Hm... What can I tell you that hasn't been told a hundred times... Heard about Yantar? No? Something blew up there, about a year ago. So hard you could hear it all the way at the Cordon. Don't know what exactly it was, but it wiped out every living thing there. Whatever it was, being there became... scary. I sent a squad there once, for recon, and they came back almost crying from fear. And I've heard the same from other stalkers, so I'll take their word for it. But the strangest thing is, after that boom, people started seeing strange stalkers around the Zone, wearing suits nobody's ever seen before. And they say these guys walk around humming something under their breath... like some kind of church hymns, only really creepy and incomprehensible... It's all one murky story, in short. I don't recommend you poke your nose in there, soldier boy, unless you want to join them.
Listen, back when I used to listen to the radio, I loved tuning in to the "100 Rads" frequency, they always played great tracks. But now I can't catch it at all, just static. Do you know why?
Well, there's no Bar anymore, and nobody's running that frequency.
Uh... What do you mean, there's no Bar?!
Oh-ho-ho, where have you been the last couple of years, bro?
In Pripyat, then on the Big Land. I don't know much about how things work in the Zone now...

No surprise there. Don't tell me you haven't heard about Varta either? Hah, you're something else! Alright, then listen to this story: about 2 years ago, right when they were shutting down the Brain Scorcher, a huge scandal broke out in Duty. Their general back then, Voronin, went completely rotten: sent his own men to the slaughter, did some business with bandits, and was a real piece of shit. It all came out when somebody leaked the info of one of the bandits he was working with. Obviously, a lot of people in Duty weren't happy. The faction basically split in two. One part stayed loyal to Voronin, and the other broke away and decided to create a "new and righteous Duty". They called themselves Varta and went off to the Valley to build up their new faction. And it was led by General Voronin's own son, imagine the family drama there, huh?
Interesting...

It gets even more interesting. For a while Varta was gaining strength, and you know, I liked those guys! Unlike Duty, they actually brought order wherever they were, they weren't arrogant bastards, and they respected ordinary stalkers. They even made peace with Freedom, can you imagine?! At some point it seemed like Varta and Duty would see eye to eye and make up... But no. Duty got weaker every day, and one fine day the son decided to finish off the father: he gathered a huge squad and marched on Rostok. The slaughter that day was terrible. Even though Shaggy, Varta's leader, gave everyone a chance to leave who didn't want to die for Duty's rotten ideals, many stayed. Even some free stalkers who were resting there at the time joined the defense of the Bar. But it was no use: all the defenders fell that day, and General Voronin, rumor has it, was shot by his own son. And that was the end of the "100 Rads" Bar. Varta, of course, didn't stop stalkers from taking Rostok back and reopening the place... But nobody dared. Since then the factory has become one of the most dangerous places south of the Brain Scorcher. The whole place is littered with anomalies, mutants and corpses from that very slaughter. Even seasoned stalkers try to steer clear of that dead place. And Varta itself... vanished. A lot of people saw them going back to the Dark Valley, but then... They disappeared off the face of the earth. Left their main base, pulled all their patrols and checkpoints, took their gear... and left. Where to? Nobody knows. Though I do have some guesses... But let's talk about that another time.
I really missed a lot...
And who's that guy sitting outside your base?
What guy? All of us stay within this building, nobody sticks their nose out. Could be one of Fanatic's people, of course, but I really doubt it.
He's sitting by the campfire, right here around the corner. He seemed strange to me, too...
What's the guy's name?
No idea, he didn't introduce himself. A guy around 50-60, in a cloak, with a beard, I think. Talks in riddles, kept dodging the subject.
Hm... Don't know anybody like that. And I'm not picking up anyone new on my PDA contacts either. Maybe you imagined it?
What are you doing here?

Trying to survive, what else! We're diggers, soldier. We dig through junk piles, undergrounds and catacombs, trying to haul out anything of value. And lately we've also been, part-time, fighters for justice. After what happened at the Bar and at Yantar, the Zone basically split in two. Rarely does anyone try to go further, up North, let alone come back. And down South, lately, there's such shit going on, you can't even imagine...
Actually, I can. The colonel told me that all the military posts and bases in the Zone are dealing with a ton of problems right now. And ours is no exception.

Well, it's not just you. So we're trying to fight this... something. We help stalkers survive when we can. "Fighting the darkness", goddammit. So far without much success, though, and with heavy losses...
And what keeps you here personally? Why not just leave for the Big Land?

Hm... I used to live at the Garbage, tried to be a kind of link between the Bar and the rest of the South. Only that drew a lot of attention from the local bandits, we had constant skirmishes with them. Once they drove us into such a hole... If it weren't for the help of one Duty guy, Bullet, we'd have croaked for sure, broke as we were. He helped us a lot back then. And then my friend Mole called me here. He used to run the stalkers here and was counting on my help. And since he disappeared on one of the runs to Yantar, now I'm in charge here. I can't just walk away without doing my duty... Heh, Bullet taught me that: stay true to your goal and don't stray from the path. So until we clear Agroprom of the "darkness", I'm not leaving. Although, looking at how things are going, nobody's getting out of here alive... Nobody except those who control the "darkness" itself...
No more questions.
I won't keep you, serviceman.
Hey, army boy, sure, we've got a truce, but don't you try anything funny. Keep quiet, and you won't have any trouble.
Lieutenant, our clients are in place, your move now. I'll be waiting for you with the goodies
Supply crate
An army crate with ammo and medical supplies for the garrison checkpoints.
Colonel's case
A sealed case. The colonel told you to give it to Seriy and not to ask what's inside.
Bandit's PDA

A worn PDA. One entry in the notes: "Man, can you fuckin' believe this. They put me out for a meet with the army like some total sucker. Vasyan says, just stand there, shoot the shit, they'll bring the cash, and we'll be around the corner. And if the soldiers start shooting first, who catches it? That's right, me, motherfucker! They're sitting in the bushes jerking off, and they stuck me out here like a fuckin' moron in an open field. 25 grand, they say, we'll split it between everybody. Yeah, right, they'll split it. If I get whacked, there's more for them. No ammo for these pigs, obviously, nobody was ever gonna give 'em any. They show up with the cash, we waste everybody, grab the dough and bail. If only I live that long, fuck..."
Unknown stalker's PDA

A PDA in the same strange casing as the suit. Inside is a single recording, dictated in an even, calm voice: "Day twelve. Leading the burnt-out to the third post, as ordered. There are seven of them, then they gave me three more. They're quiet. They feel no fear and no pain, they just go wherever I look. I used to think this was cruel. Now I understand: it's mercy. They've already given everything they could, and Horus found them one last use. The task is not to take the post. The task is to watch. Who shoots, who runs, who freezes and listens. The brother said that at every post there's at least one who hears. Don't touch him. Mark him. The soldiers there are angry and hungry, but anger is just fear that hasn't found where to go yet. Someday it will. We'll wait. Liberation will come for everyone..."
Boy of da baze garrizun. WAAAAGH!
Soldier of an Agroprom Research Institute garrison checkpoint.
Head of an Agroprom Research Institute garrison checkpoint.
Bandit.
Zombified.
Head of the diggers at the factory. Used to live at the Garbage.
