How can I help you?

There's one little problem here. Not long ago a group of my people went down into the depths of the Agroprom underground, looking for something... The guys never came back, we waited 3 days for them. But we managed to pick up a weak signal coming from the upper levels of the underground. We never dared to check it, though, didn't want to show our faces around you guys more than we have to... Maybe you know something about it?

Actually, I was there recently, and I saw the body of a digger, probably one of yours. He died shooting it out with some stalkers I don't know. I've never seen suits like the ones they were wearing in my life, not even the Monolith fanatics have those. The dead man's buddies attacked me soon after and nearly finished me off. On one of them I found a PDA with audio recordings. Listen.

Yeah, too bad about the guys. How many have I gotten killed already, huh?... I send people to their deaths and sit here acting like a big shot... Alright, I'll reflect later. Here, take this, thanks for avenging the guys. And hand over the PDA, I'll try to dig some useful info out of it. And for now... I've got one more request for you.
Go on.

I've heard about these unknown stalkers for a long time, and it's not the first time I've lost people to their guns. Me and the guys keep trying to crack their riddle: who they are, what they want, who's in charge, and so on down the list. I think these questions bother you military guys too. I'd bet my teeth your commanders have run into these bastards more than once. So by helping us, you'll help yourself. We managed to find out a few things, but far from everything. The main info will come from our scouts, who are about to come back from dead Yantar. Can you meet them and escort them to the base? They absolutely have to survive, every man counts here. Can you handle it?
Why not send your own people? You're ready to trust a soldier?
Ahem... There's a good reason for that, I'll tell you if you come back with my people. That's it, go on, they'll be there soon. I sent the coordinates to your PDA.
Don't shoot, stalker! I'm from Seriy, I'm on your side...
Hah, and why the hell should I believe you?! What if you're one of those... crazies with the "eyes"...
I can contact him, he'll confirm it. Seriy said you need an escort to the base, said you've got important info on the unknown stalkers.

Hm... Well, he's got a point. Hah, didn't think he did business with the military, but since we're already in this deep shit, it'd be a sin not to... Alright, soldier, you've convinced me. Heading to the base?
Lead the way, stalker... Uh, guys, what are you doing? Lower your gu...
What the hell was that setup just now?!
Get a grip, soldier boy! Gun down, and stop yelling! What happened out there? Where are the scouts?!
Your "scouts" attacked me!
Wha?...

There were four of them. I came up to talk to one, everything seemed fine, we were about to leave, and then the other three opened fire on us. The guy I was talking to was killed instantly, and only by some miracle I managed to take out the rest.
Goddammit... And what about the PDA? He should've had a PDA on him!
That PDA's fucked, one of the bullets went straight through it. Here, have a look.
Oh, fuck me... One setup after another! And more losses in the squad, damn it... Alright, sorry I yelled, my nerves are at the limit already. Take this, a little compensation for your trouble.
No offense taken. Now tell me everything you know about this new faction, why I was attacked, and what the hell is going on here?

They call themselves "the Order". They showed up in the Zone recently. About a year ago people started seeing them in large numbers in the south, though rumors about these "cultists" were going around back in '12. They recruit people from all the factions of the Zone: Freedom, Loners, Bandits, Varta. That last one has most likely gone over to them entirely. Serious guys, they shoot without warning, to kill. Their goals... who the hell knows what their goals are, they don't put up posters with their slogans. But they're not your typical fanatics, like the ones you might've seen in Monolith or Sin. They're... sane, or something. Most of them joined voluntarily, and they serve not because some mysterious miracle machine is frying their brains, but of their own free will.
What a mess...

Looks like my scouts fell victim to their indoctrination and decided to go over to the Order's side. God, how long were they serving them? Since they were sent on the mission? That's months of them...
Now I get why you didn't want to send your people. You were afraid of betrayal. Only you were looking in the wrong direction, it turns out.

Couldn't have said it better. Bottom line: the Order is a serious threat... not just to us or you, but to the whole Zone as such, its laws, its order and its rules. And if we sit on our hands, we'll lose for sure. We have to do something, or they'll crush us like pathetic bugs...

Tell me, Lieutenant, we're not the only ones who've started noticing strange things around Agroprom, are we? Terrible wailing from the swamps, people going missing, headaches of all kinds, more zombie activity, panic attacks... I'm right, aren't I?

Yes, it's not just you. Our whole garrison is moping and raving like the end of the world is coming tomorrow... You know, I'm actually a medic by trade, they only recently transferred me to the infantry. And in all my time on the job I've never seen anything like it. And the most interesting part: for no apparent reason. Something is definitely wrong here, but I just can't figure out what exactly.

That's what we've been trying to figure out for months now. Can't say we've had much success... There used to be about fifty of us at this base, and now... well, you can see for yourself how many of us are left. Those guys are far from the first to fall under the Order's influence, and I'm afraid they're far from the last.

Hm... We've had cases where soldiers left their post or just dissolved into the darkness. Only later they were seen alive, in the distance, and as soon as someone tried to get closer, they'd quickly walk away. Looks like you've got something similar...

Listen, if we want to do something about this, we need to figure out if the "fallen" have any signs, symptoms maybe, call it what you want. If we find out what pushes them to betray, maybe we can prevent it in the future. Those guys coming from Yantar were from Fanatic's group. He's here, in the next building. Try asking him about the dead guys, maybe he noticed something strange in how they acted.
That makes sense, I'll go talk to him.
Hello. Are you Fanatic? Seriy sent me, he said you could tell me about your guys... the ones coming from Yantar.
I've heard about the mess already, the whole camp's buzzing. So you're that army doctor. And I can see it's been a long day for you. How are you holding up, Lieutenant?
I've been better, to be honest. So, about your guys?

They were good lads. All four of them were mine, I trained them myself back when I was at the Cordon. Calm, not greedy, didn't talk too much. A shame, of course. But you know... everyone in the Zone finds their place. Some sooner, some later. So they found theirs.
Hm... That's a peculiar way to talk about the dead.

And how else should I talk about them? Tears won't raise the dead. I've been here a very long time, I've learned to accept things as they come. And they always come the right way, Lieutenant, even when it seems like they don't... Better tell me how things are at your base. There are all sorts of rumors going around. They say your people are leaving?
%c[fr_control]That's classified information, stalker, I can't answer that.
%c[fr_chaos]Yeah, they're leaving. Sometimes lone patrols, and sometimes whole squads go missing. Downright mystical.
I see. Well, you army guys are tough. You're tough yourself, I can see. You've been walking around so much today and you're still on your feet. That's good. That'll come in handy.

Don't be sad, soldier, everything will work out. It's always been like that in the Zone: first it's a total shitshow, and then it's good... And you army guys are tough anyway. You're tough yourself, I can see. You've been walking around so much today and you're still on your feet. That's good. That'll come in handy.
...Come in handy for what?

For life, what else. *smirks* Alright, I won't keep you, Seriy's waiting, I suppose. Oh, listen, wait a second. Since you're walking between the base and us anyway... I've got a five-minute job, good for both of us. Interested?
What kind of job?

Seriy threw us a job, and before it we need to restock our gear. And my lads, may they rest... they left a stash in the underground before they left. On the upper level, not far from the anomaly tunnel. You probably know it, you've been there. If I go poking around there, well, you understand, your soldiers won't take it well. But you're one of them, you're allowed. Bring it back and we'll split it fair and square: half for you for the legwork, half for me for the tip. Deal?
Hm, makes sense... And what's in the stash?

Ammo and meds, a little of everything, enough for our group. Maybe a gun's lying there, I don't remember anymore. I sent the mark to your PDA. Only, Lieutenant... don't make too much noise down there, alright?
What do you mean, don't make noise? Is somebody down there?
Who could be down there. Rats and darkness. It's just an omen we have, us diggers: don't make noise in echoing places. The Zone loves silence. See you, Lieutenant.
Will you tell me a bit about yourself?
Not much to tell, I'm a simple man. Well, ask away, if you're curious.
How's life here in the camp?

Life's alright. We've got a roof, the loot keeps coming, Seriy's a fair man, he won't wrong you for nothing. Others whine: not enough food, it's scary, they want to go home. But why whine? You always want to go home, but none of us has a home, that's why we're all sitting in the Zone. Everything's running its course. Everything's... going the right way, Lieutenant.
You're from the Cordon, right? How did you end up here?

From the Cordon, yeah. After Wolf, I carried the village on my back, led the rookies, taught them not to walk into anomalies. Good times, only empty. Then I realized it's not for me, wiping kids' snotty noses. I wanted... meaning, I guess. A real cause. Joined up with Seriy, and here... I found what I was looking for, you could say. More than I was looking for.
Haven't noticed anything strange around here?

Strange? No, I guess not. The Zone's the Zone, it's always been strange, from day one. People are afraid because they don't understand. And once you understand, there's nothing to be afraid of. Nothing at all.
Alright, thanks.
Anytime. I'm here.
Here's the crate, found it, picked it up, no problems. It's quiet down there... Too quiet, even.
Well, it's a dead-end underground, what's there to make noise? Hand it over, let me open it... Done. Look, I'll let you pick from this crate: restock your ammo, or take some meds. Pick one.
I'll take the meds.
Give me the ammo.
That's good. You know how to listen, Lieutenant, that's rare. You'll go far. Here, and something on top, a little gift from me. Now my group is ready for the trip.
Thanks. Though wouldn't you need it more?
No, soldier, where we're going, we won't need artifacts at all. Go in peace.
Scout's PDA
PDA of a stalker from Seriy's group. During the firefight it was pierced by a large-caliber bullet and, in effect, destroyed. The data is unreadable, the device is beyond repair.
Fanatic's cache
A crate the stalker group stashed before leaving. Inside are ammo and medical supplies.
Northern checkpoint
Scout
Reporting in, Colonel.
What have you got? Did you find the PDA?
Yes and no. The scout really was dead, he was killed by zombified stalkers.
Zombies here? Are you... sure?

I saw their kind in Pripyat. Only these were different... I don't even know how to describe it properly. The "old" zombies had no purpose in mind: just leftover motor skills, scraps of habits, an empty stare. The shells of former people just wandered around the Zone, a truly pathetic sight. But the ones I met here... They're aggressive, tough killing machines. When I was approaching the scout, the zombies kept shooting at his body, nonstop... They riddled the poor kid completely, there wasn't a single spot left untouched. As if someone gave them an order, and they kept carrying it out to the very end.
Damn it...
The PDA, as you've probably guessed, was ruined by the hail of bullets.
If what you're saying is true, then we're deep in the shit, Lieutenant... And this isn't the first time you've run into zombies like that in combat, is it?
Affirmative. When I was helping the third checkpoint, a group of those creatures attacked us. We fought them off, but that's not the main thing. They had a "leader".
What do you mean?

After the fight I found a stalker from a faction I don't know. I've run into ones like him before, in the underground beneath our base. I assume you know they show up here often too... This stalker acted unusual in combat: he was clearly conscious, and, it seemed to me, he was commanding those zombies. He was their "shepherd".
Hm... That explains a lot... So the zombies that attacked the scout got their orders from the same kind of shepherd?
I'm leaning toward that theory. But I didn't see anyone nearby. I think the "shepherd" gave the order and left. What happened to the "herd" after that didn't interest him.
So that's why they kept following the order even after the scout was dead, there were no other instructions... Understood, Lieutenant, that clears a lot up. Do you know anything about their faction?

The stalker Seriy, from the factory, told me about them. Name: the Order. Goals unknown, numbers unknown too, but I think more than a hundred. Organized like a conscious cult. Actively recruiting fighters, aggressive. He promised to tell me more if I keep helping him.

*lowers his voice* Fuck... Fucked-up cultists, that's all we needed... *raises his voice* Fine, then you take care of this. The stalkers clearly know more about them than we do, so let them share that knowledge with you. As soon as you figure something out, come straight to me. And in the meantime I'll try to deal with the zombie problem, before they flood all of Agroprom. We'll try to figure out where they're coming from... And you're dismissed for now, Rogovets.
Colonel, sir, one more thing...
Go ahead.
What happened to the northern checkpoint? I thought we were supposed to have guards there, but there's nobody there...
What?!
Well... at the northern checkpoint... there are no people.
Motherfucking son of a bitch... Are you ABSOLUTELY sure about that?!
Absolutely, Colonel.
*heavy sigh* It just keeps getting worse... Now this plague has reached the main base too. What the fuck are you supposed to do... Might as well start tearing my hair out from despair...

Alright, Rogovets, don't just stand there like a post, this isn't your concern anymore. You can drop by the quartermaster, he was looking for you, I think... *starts muttering to himself* I'll have to send another squad there, from the reserve, to plug the hole in the defense. But who? And is it even worth it? Everyone's headed down the same road anyway...

Rogovets, you're at the stalker camp right now, so you're the closest: west of that complex my scout's signal went dead, he was carrying important intel for me. I don't have much hope, so your job is to take the PDA from him... off him, and bring it to the base.
The post is empty... No guards, no signs of a fight. Where did they all go?
Scout's PDA
A military scout's PDA. Riddled with bullets, the data can't be recovered.
Scout of the Agroprom Research Institute garrison.
Hello, you wanted to see me?

Yeah, let's get straight to business. First: the colonel ordered me to give you a small reward for doing your assignments well, keep it up. And now, about my request. I'll keep it short. About a week ago one of our patrols went missing, and my little brother was in it... I lost hope very quickly and soon accepted that he was dead. But now I keep hearing more and more often that zombies are showing up more and more. And a thought crept into my head: what if my little brother isn't dead, but is still wandering out there, among them... You haven't by any chance seen... any of ours among the zombies?
No, I haven't. I'd definitely recognize my patients.

Hm... Lieutenant, if you see any, then... well, you know what's usually done with them, but... if you see any of the "former" guys, and you see one of them with a heavy machine gun... then lay his soul to rest, please. As proof, bring me back that machine gun. I have to be sure he won't wander the Zone for the rest of his life as an empty shell of himself... Nobody deserves that fate.
I understand, Sergeant. I'll do as you ask.
It's about the machine gun.
Yeah, yeah, thank you, Lieutenant... Hand it over. Let's sort out your reward now...
You're not even going to ask how I found it, who I took it from?

I won't ask. I know where you got it, I heard Kuznetsov's orders. I've known for a long time that my little brother... that he's not alive, but... hope dies last, right? That's enough, I don't want to think about it any more than I have to...
I understand, I'm sorry.
Well, his machine gun will serve us, the living, loyally and faithfully, agreed? And so you don't get sad, here, take a Kriss Vector and all the ammo we have for it. Now leave me alone, please...
I'm back.

Took you long enough, soldier boy. What happened over there? You flew out of that building like you'd been scalded and ran off somewhere, I didn't even get a chance to shout anything. And then shooting started all around...
Colonel's orders, there was another attack... I wanted to go back to Fanatic and talk to him again, but...
You're too late, friend, Fanatic already left on my job, should've come sooner. Did you manage to find out anything from him at least?

You know... not much. He mentioned his guys in a few words, then dodged the question and started asking me questions himself. Then he even sent me to fetch a stash, even split the reward with me. Long story short, I didn't learn anything useful.
That's lousy, brother, lousy...

Listen, how long has Fanatic been with you? I don't want to sound paranoid and accuse everyone of betrayal, but... I don't like him. He's too... sickly sweet and calm. Everyone else here is on pins and needles, but this guy...

Long enough for me to trust him with half the group. I've known him since the Cordon, we came to the Zone around the same time. Fate split us up, but after the shake-up in '12, after Duty's beating down in the South... We got back together and settled here. He's a simple, calm guy, that's what I like about him, he keeps his composure even in a situation like this.

It's just that I felt uneasy around him... You know, I've been to Pripyat. The guys joke that I came back shell-shocked. I was under psy-strikes a couple of times and survived. And ever since this... devilry started here, that Pripyat "gut feeling" of mine just won't go away... And what about...

*gets a PDA signal* Oh, wait, I think I know what this is... Yes, excellent! Right, I need to set this up now... Listen, soldier boy, I've got one small request for you: go to our radio operator, get 3 PVM-14 devices from him and come back to me, I'll tell you what to do with them. Trust me, this will help us in the fight against the Order!
I don't like these sudden requests. Alright, I'll be right back.
SOS, SOS, this is the 2nd patrol, we need help, we're under attack!
This is the 3rd squad, we've been attacked by zombies, we need help!
1st here, a wave of zombies is moving toward us, send reinforcements!
...we're done... don't come here....
There are too many of them....
Hold on, men... We have t...
We fought them off, men, good work. Not without losses, but we fought them off. The survivors fell back to the base.
The camp is empty. No casings, no blood. Am I too late?.. Or were they never here at all. Quiet... Like at the northern post.
Cultist's PDA

Points 1-4 on schedule. The herd is fresh, just came in from Fulgrim yesterday. Total expenditure is acceptable. After that, to the cache in the trailer at the factory, to restock. And how did those stalker idiots not spot me from the windows? And the cache is important, it resupplies our groups here...
Are you all fucking out of your minds here or what?!
What are you talking about?
Your radio operator is dead! The body's already gone cold, I found no signs of violence. The devices weren't on him.
How could this... How long has he been like this?..
I don't know, but at least a few hours.
Fuck... How many have I gotten killed like this... And now the devices are gone. This is a total disaster!
What was your plan exactly? Why do you need these devices?

We wanted to pull off some tricks with the radio towers at Agroprom, and then we'd be able to pick up the Order's PDA signals from a long distance. The devices would've let us do that, but now... No, there's always hope! Listen, LT, he was definitely murdered, he couldn't have just...
I understand it wasn't a heart attack. But I didn't see any bullet or knife wounds either. I don't rule out a psy-strike.

Shit... Listen, the killer couldn't have gone far, he's still somewhere around Agroprom. I'm sure he's from the Order, only they could pull off something like this and take the devices without drawing attention. Your job is to track him down and finish him off. If you find the devices, come straight to me. In the meantime I'll contact my people and try to find that bastard too.
Just don't let our patrols see you. We're in a nasty mood these days.
Captain, sir, Lieutenant Rogovets. Reporting for duty.

Ah, the medic... I've heard about you. They say you're carrying everyone's load around here: dragging patrols out, roaming the factory with stalkers. Good thing you came, an extra gun won't hurt today.
What do we know about the enemy?

Not much. They've dug in at a fortified point by the road to Yantar. Twenty to thirty zombies there, maybe more. Recon saw someone in a robe among them, looks like their shepherd. And... they saw ours. In uniform.
Ours?

Former ours. Don't pity them, Lieutenant, nothing can help them anymore. Here's how we work: we move as one group, push from the front, take out the shepherd first, without him the herd turns into a mob. You stay close to me, don't wander off. And if any of my guys get hit, you patch them up on the move. Questions?
No questions.
Then let's go. Squad, forward! Move out!
Copy that!
Colonel, sir...
Speak.

I joined Captain Akeran's group, and we started the assault. At first everything went according to plan: we advanced smoothly, pushed the zombies back without much trouble. In the center of their camp stood another shepherd, and around him was an escort of... our former soldiers. Zombified too, they acted like the rest. Not without losses, but we killed them all.
Go on.

The captain ordered us to search the bodies. On the shepherd I found a note, and at that very second I felt a psy-effect, the same as in Pripyat. I'm resistant to that, I came to quickly. And then Akeran saw soldiers coming toward us. The same ones who went missing from the northern post.

He called out to them, he was even glad... And then a voice sounded in my head: "Fulfill your purpose!" And the "lost ones" opened fire. The captain was killed first. We managed to kill them, but the losses are heavy...

*long pause* I put them on the missing list... I thought, we'll find the bodies, I'll write to their mothers: "died in the line of duty"... And what am I supposed to write now, Lieutenant? "Your son gunned down our garrison and was then killed by his own"? Right under our noses... They're stealing soldiers right from under our noses, and sending back... this... And Akeran. He was a good officer.
Colonel, sir, one more thing. The voice... the one that talked about "purpose". I heard it too. It spoke to me as well. I just... didn't get up.
And what does that mean, medic?

I don't know, Colonel. Maybe there was a thin layer between me and the fallen... or maybe Pripyat did this to me. I can't say for sure. And there's this, the note. Read it. They knew we were coming. The camp by the road was bait.
*reads* ...Need the reserve on the northern post... though what reserve... It doesn't matter anyway... we're all going to die here.
Colonel, sir?..

As you were. Now, here are your orders, Lieutenant. We need to pull every reserve we have back to the base. Enough feeding these bastards piece by piece. If they want to destroy us, let them come and try! I'll give the order to shut down all our operations at Agroprom, in a few hours all units will fall back here, to the main base. And I'm giving you a special assignment. You've built a good rapport with the stalkers at the factory, it seems... I don't care how, but you have to bring them here. Tell Seriy to pack up his camp and bring his group to us. We'll provide everything we can. Is your task clear?
Crystal clear. Permission to ask: why do we need them here?

We have a common enemy, that should already be enough. On our own they'll just pick us off or turn us to their side, and the more guns we have here, the better. What's more, I need to ask Seriy a few questions personally. The main thing is to buy time... Now, why are you still here? Carry out your orders!
Yes, sir!
Colonel Kuznetsov
Captain Akeran
Lieutenant Rogovets

All posts, this is Colonel Kuznetsov. We've established where the zombie attacks were coming from: they've taken the fortified point by the road to Yantar. Our task is to strike back and destroy the enemy.
Captain Akeran's squad will handle the sweep. All soldiers in the vicinity, I order you to join the strike group. Good luck, boys.
Excellent work, men, the enemy is destroyed! Search the bodies, there might be something important.
I see movement... What's that... ours?.. Hey, it's the guys from the northern checkpoint!
Guys, where the hell have you been?!
%c[fr_chaos]Fulfill your purpose!
Hey, what are you doing?! Lower your weap-...
Colonel, sir, this is Lieutenant Rogovets, over.
Report, Lieutenant.
Captain Akeran's squad and I attacked the zombie camp and destroyed it. But soon after that we were hit from behind, and by our own!
It was the missing soldiers from the northern checkpoint. The captain is KIA, the squad took heavy losses...
What are your orders, Colonel?
Colonel, sir, over?..
.........Return to base, Lieutenant.
Dead... No blood, no wounds. And the devices aren't on him.
Captain Akeran
Commander of the Agroprom Research Institute garrison assault group. An experienced officer, not his first year in the Zone.
Shepherd's note

A sheet of paper folded in four, covered in even, almost calligraphic handwriting:

To the shepherd of the herd by the road.
Keep the herd at the point. The soldiers will come, the colonel will not stand for it. Let all he can gather come, do not hinder them. Your flesh will become your last service to the Order, and it will be accepted.
Keep the radio operator's devices on you. The brother will collect them afterward.
The warriors from the northern outpost await the Voice. When the Voice calls, they will fulfill their purpose.
The Eye sees.
PVM-14 device
A compact receiver-repeater in a protected casing. Seriy planned to mount these on the old radio relay towers. There were three of them, and all three turned up on the shepherd.
Machine gunner's body
Is it just me, or are there fewer of you every time I come here?

You're observant. In other times I'd chalk it up to the Zone, but now... The guys just vanish for good. Or they step outside the camp perimeter, and that's it, they don't answer calls. But enough of the poetry. I heard gunfire north of the factory, what kind of party did you have over there?
A lot happened. I can't share the details, military secret. But I've got something interesting, especially for you... *shows the devices*
No way! Where did you get them?! From whom?
Long story, but in short: the Order had them, just like you thought.
Excellent! Those bastards paid for the death of our radio operator... But this is only the beginning of our revenge! Now we need to install these devices...

Not so fast, stalker. I have orders from Colonel Kuznetsov: all stalkers in the Agroprom area must immediately pack up their camps and report to our base to reinforce the garrison. This is for your own safety, so I'm asking you to comply and not ask unnecessary questions...

Hah, orders for us, simple stalkers? Are you out of your mind, soldier boy?.. Look at us now, the army's inviting stalkers under its wing. You know, any other day I'd laugh my ass off. But not today. Sorry, Lieutenant, but I can't. At least not until I've done my duty, until I finish what I started...
What are you talking about?

Those devices we've been looking for so long... They're the key to our victory over the Order, understand! With them we'll see them all... Every cultist, their every step. I... no, WE have to do this, Lieutenant. And you're going to help us.
Seriy, I have orders...

I don't give a shit about your orders! I already did my time in the army, none of your people gets to boss me around anymore! Understand, if we do this, it'll only be better for you! We'll share the software with you that'll track their coordinates. The Order will crumble in the blink of an eye! Trust me, soldier...
*deep sigh* And what exactly do you want to do?

There are three long-range radio relay towers at Agroprom, standing since Soviet times. There used to be lots of those all over the Zone, but after so many years only a few survived. These towers are line-of-sight, the antennas face each other, that's how the signal was sent. When the Union fell, the towers went silent, but the hardware's still standing! The masts are intact, the feeders... well, the power cables... are alive in places. I checked.
And what do your devices have to do with it?

Every PDA, even in sleep mode, leaks signal: service packets, a beacon, syncing, all kinds of crap. A weak signal, a hundred or two meters. But if you hang our device on a tower, it works like an ear: picks up that noise, amplifies it through the tower's antenna array and sends it to my terminal. One tower is one ear. Two, and you can roughly figure out the direction. And three, set up in a triangle: triangulation, Lieutenant, ever learn that in school? Three ears hear one PDA from three sides, and our little program calculates the point. A kilometer of coverage, accurate to a couple of meters.
And what if they don't carry PDAs?

You're catching on. Only they're all former stalkers. And what stalker goes around without a PDA? They're people, after all. Seduced, but still people... They need communication themselves, coordination. How else do you run an army? So their strength will become their weakness. Get it now?
...Alright. Let's say so. I still don't like this idea. But on the other hand, it could actually work... What do you need from me?

One antenna is right here, at the base. The second is in the forest, not far from your base. The third is in the swamp, mounted right on top of a trailer. Keep the devices for now, you got them. My guys are preparing the masts here and in the forest right now, testing the feeders. As soon as they're done, we'll mount them. And you get the swamp, with the third device. As soon as they're all running and the towers sync up, we'll have a full view of the whole Agroprom area, and then...
What is it?
You hear that?.. Somebody's walking under the base. But I haven't sent anyone yet... This is bad news.
I don't hear anyth-
And who the hell are you? Freeze, hands up, don't move!
Easy, easy, serviceman. Don't wave your gun around in a cramped space, you'll hit the antenna, and you still need it.
Wait... It's you? You were sitting by the campfire, at the factory! What are you doing here, how did you even get in here?

I was sitting there. And you were in a hurry. You're all in a hurry. Stalkers, soldiers, bandits... You don't know where you're going yourselves, but you're in a hurry. I let you go back then because you weren't ready to listen yet. And now, I see, the day has worn you down.
Who the fuck are you? Answer me!
We haven't met. No, wait, that's a lie. I know you, Lieutenant Rogovets. You don't know me. Yet.
How do you know me?

Lower your rifle. If I wanted to kill you, you'd never have made it to this trailer. You walked through my swamps, through my anomalies, under my eyes. And you made it here in one piece. Think about why.
...You're one of them. The Order.
One of them? Heh... No, serviceman, I'm not one of them. I am them. My name is Horus. The name won't tell you anything, but you've already heard it, you just didn't know you were hearing it.
Horus... That dead cultist in the underground, he talked about some Fulgrim...

Fulgrim is mine. Like that fallen brother, like the ones who shot at your checkpoint, like the ones who came back from the northern post. All mine. You've understood everything right, Lieutenant, you're a smart man, only very quiet. Quiet all your life.
You... You were waiting here on purpose? You knew I'd come?

I knew. Seriy's a clever one, he came up with a good thing. Three towers, triangulation, every cultist like a firefly on the map... He's even almost right. Install your device, I won't get in your way.
Sure, and then what? You shoot me in the back, and that's it?

If I wanted to shoot you in the back, I already would have. That's not why I'm here. I came to talk. You feel it yourself, that things here aren't so simple. You feel more than the others, you've felt it ever since Pripyat. You're just afraid to admit it to yourself.
Don't try to mess with my head, I don't fall for that!
In the clearing. When your men grabbed their heads. You heard the voice. You heard ME. And you didn't get up.

Do you know how many people have heard me in two years? Hundreds. All of them heard and went. And you stood there with your rifle and watched your own shoot at your own. That's when I decided I had to talk to you in person. People like you are rare. People like you aren't thrown away.
You... you wanted to get into my head. Like you did with them.
I didn't want to, I tried. But I couldn't... You'd have made an excellent fighter, if you hadn't spent your whole life patching up people who don't give a damn about you.
I don't care what you think of me. You killed the radio operator. You slaughtered the checkpoints. You're... a bastard.

Me? Lieutenant, let's be honest, since it's just the two of us in this tin can. Who transferred you to the infantry? A doctor who shoots worse than a recruit? Who sent you alone, with crates, all over Agroprom, knowing people were disappearing? Who told you to deliver the case and not ask what was inside? You didn't ask. But I'll tell you. Artifacts were in there. Payment. Your colonel bought people from Seriy so they'd go down below. To where several squads had already disappeared before. Those poor servicemen stayed down there, you'll see them yet. Then he sent the stalkers, and they're lying down there too. And now he'll send you... Do you understand, serviceman? You've already been sold. They just haven't written the check yet.
You're lying...
Check it. Ask Seriy what was in the case. Ask where Fanatic's group went. Just come back alive to ask.
........What do you want from me?

Finally, the right question! Tell me, soldier, what do YOU want? Not what's written in your oath. Your own. All these years in the Zone you've been patching up people who call you a burden. They say it to your face: medic, wimp, step aside, don't get in the men's way. In Pripyat you almost got your team killed, and you still sleep with that. Nobody listens to you. Not the colonel, not the sergeant in the underground, not this stalker with his antennas. And do you know who heard you for the first time in all these years? I did. Through the swamp, through half a kilometer, through your Pripyat pain, I heard you.

I'll give you what you've never had. Strength. Not this tin can in your hands, real strength. People who will follow you and never ask why. A voice that people listen to. You won't be patching rotten boards, you'll be building something new. And you'll never have to ask permission to breathe from a colonel who has already written you off.
You want me... to betray my own?

Your own? Lieutenant, look around! Your generals sell out their soldiers, your superiors cut you down like cattle, because someone up there decided the Zone isn't needed anymore. Your colonel pays with artifacts for other people's lives. Where are your own here? Your own are the ones who stood firm, the ones who heard and didn't go. People like you. And people like me.
Haven't I already killed enough of your fighters? Why are you even talking to me?

Most of them, the wild ones and the zombies, are expendable to me. Those who believed, but not sincerely... Those who listened with half an ear... Or those who refused to believe, or betrayed us. And the living fighters of the Order who fell fighting you... Clearly they turned out weaker than you. And if they're weaker than you, what use are they to the Order? If you accept my offer, you'll pay for their deaths tenfold.
And if I refuse?

Then you'll install your device, come down from the swamp, and watch everything you defended today crumble in your hands. Not because I want to punish you, not at all. Because it's already crumbling, you just haven't watched it to the end yet. I'm offering you not to wait for the end. I'm offering you to make it.
I won't pressure you. I never pressure, it's your commanders who pressure. I just ask and offer. But only once. Will you come with me?
%c[fr_chaos]I.......... will come.

...I wasn't wrong about you. Leave the device, you won't need it anymore. Let Seriy believe in his triangulation a little longer, he doesn't have long left to believe. Go, Lieutenant. They're waiting for you... They've been waiting a long time.
Where to?..
To where you'll finally be heard. Go.
%c[fr_control]No.

No. I'm Lieutenant Rogovets, a military doctor, and I'm loyal to my oath. And I've seen the price people pay for your "strength". Mindless zombies in the clearing who have no purpose left... Or savages with blood in their eyes, with wild, insatiable rage and fury, whose only purpose is to kill... No, Horus, I don't need that. Not for any strength.
...A pity. Truly a pity, soldier, I rarely say that.
You'll live. Now get out of my way!
I don't make offers twice, Rogovets. Remember that. The next time we meet, I won't be offering.
I said, get out of my way!
Greetings, battle brother. I'm glad to see you've made the right choice.
What do I have to do?
The Prophet said you're the one we need. He was right. Not everyone could mow down so many of the "burnt-out" and stay alive. Take this. It's the best thing you've ever worn.
I... This is excellent gear.
The best. Now fulfill your purpose. Destroy the base together with us. Not one of them may leave alive. The colonel is yours personally. So said Horus.
...Understood. Let's move out.
What the fuck, who the hell are these guys?! HEL...
Fuck, not a second of peace! Guys, take defensive positions, move! Soldier, don't waste time, get up on the roof and install the first device yourself, we'll cover you!
Even more of these fucking lunatics, coming from the north!
Buddy, there's a crazy number of monsters here, help us out!
Good work, LT, but don't relax: we got an SOS from the guys in the forest, the ones who were supposed to activate the second tower, mutants attacked them.
Run over there quick and help them, and we'll finish off these lunatics in the meantime.
Thanks for coming! Now we'll kick their asses!
Excellent, soldier, excellent: we've got a signal from the second tower. Just one little thing left: hook up the last one, the third, out in the swamp.
Looks like we've fought off these savages, so once you install the last device, come over to us at the base, we'll show you the full power of our new technology!
The device is in place. Now I have to hold out until it starts up.
%c[fr_chaos]One chance. One will. Let it burn.
A former stalker. Nothing in his eyes but rage.
A stalker from Seriy's camp.
Horus
Knows more than he should.
Fulgrim

Meeting point
The infirmary. Bandages for a week, painkillers for a couple of days. Who's going to treat anyone if I go down myself?
The rifle's heavier than I remember. Or my hands are out of practice... Alright, Lieutenant, orders are orders.
Damp and dark, like a crypt. The last time I went underground was back in Pripyat... Don't think about it. Not now.
Air at last. Never thought I'd be this glad to breathe this rotten air.
Just a dozen of those things, and the post is already running out of ammo. A crate for a week... If they even get that week.
Zombies? Here?... I haven't seen them since Pripyat... But these are angrier, faster, tougher. And that stalker too... As if he was leading them.
Strange guy. Calm voice, but he looked at me like he knew more about me than I do.
The stalkers shot one of their own. And this morning they sat at the same campfire... Something about this place breaks people. I just hope it doesn't break me.
Just a kid. How old was he, twenty? Twenty-two?.. How am I going to tell Kuznetsov?
The colonel's holding his head again, he's in really bad shape. The pills don't help anymore... I'll have to examine him properly. If he lets me...
First the checkpoints, now the patrols. A whole camp vanished like it was never there... They're picking us off one by one.
The captain asked them to lower their weapons. And they answered with a burst... Rest in peace, warrior.
Two of them didn't make it. Late again, Doc...
It's so quiet I can hear my heart beating. And it keeps feeling like someone's watching my back.
%c[fr_chaos]Just this morning I was bandaging these guys. And now I'm going to kill them. And I feel... calm?... Finally, I'm free.
Rogovets?! You bastard... I supplied you, and you're with them?! You're dead, got it?!
Lieutenant... You too... I vouched for you to HQ, you son of a bitch... Come on then, come here. Let's see what they taught you.
Doc... you stitched me up the day before yesterday... Why?..
Fuck... What happened? I blacked out after installing the device...
All the electronics are fucking dead. PDA, flashlight, radio, nothing works... It's all because of that antenna!
I need to get back to Seriy, now.
Freeze! Hands up! ...Rogovets, that you? You're alive?
Easy, easy, lower your gun! I'm alive, damn it... Seriy, what's going on here...
Are you alone?
Alone. What the fuck happened here?

A lot. Listen carefully, I don't have the strength to repeat myself. Right after you left, we fought off those savages almost immediately. They had rage to spare, but they died from a couple of shots. We killed them all, we'd already cleaned up the main building, and then your guys showed up. About seven of them, in military uniforms, with patches, the whole deal. They said the colonel ordered all stalkers to pack up and move under the walls of the base. And we believed them. You'd offered us the same thing yourself a couple of hours before, who'd expect a trick, especially when we have a truce? Yeah, right, fucking hell... Trusted them, and look where it got me...
Goddammit... Those weren't soldiers, were they?

What the fuck does it matter now who they were? As soon as we turned around and started packing our things, a storm of fire came down on us. Your "comrades" shot to kill, sparing no one. I got lucky: a few poor bastards were standing in front of me, they took the first volley, and by some miracle I ran off and took cover behind the crates. We fought them off, but I lost a lot of people... In fact, all the survivors are standing in front of you right now.

Fuck it all... Those were traitors, like the ones from the northern checkpoint. Horus managed to convert them to his faith. So they were sitting at the base all this time and heard the colonel's order too... How many more of them do we have?
I've got a feeling there's more Order at your base by now than actual garrison... So, what about you? Did you install the third device?

I did. Seriy, there... There was a man there. He was waiting for me in the trailer, he didn't show up on the PDA. He knew about the towers, he knew about your triangulation... He... he invited me to join him. To join the Order.
I take it that was Horus himself. Son of a bitch... You're in deep shit if the leader of those fanatics himself has his eye on you. You... shot him, right?
I thought so, yes. Only in his place there was the body of an ordinary zombie.
Yeah... And then what?
I hooked up the device, and it immediately zapped me, I blacked out. When I came to, there was thick fog outside, and all the electronics were dead: PDA, flashlight, radio...

Uh-huh... Ours too, all at once. Apparently, the very second you turned that damn thing on. It's all because of those fucking devices... You think the Order stole them from us, kept them for half a day and didn't tweak anything in them? Looks like they did something so that instead of sending a signal, it made an EMP, one so strong it covered all of Agroprom.
We handed them victory on a silver platter...
We're idiots, Lieutenant. We wanted to see, to watch their every step... And in the end we plunged ourselves into darkness.
We couldn't have known.

What does it matter now whether we could or not?... Listen, I have one last request for you. Our last hope is Fanatic's group, five people. I sent them to the railway tunnel this morning on your colonel's job, their time was up before sunset. There's no contact, and it looks like there won't be. My two won't go there, I won't let them, they're all I have left. Go, try to find them.
Will you finally tell me why the hell they went there, and on our money too?

If you come back, I'll tell you. I can already guess what happened to them, but still... Hope dies last, or however they say it in the movies? And be careful, soldier: we didn't kill all the Order guys, some of them managed to retreat. Keep your eyes open.
I have VERY bad news.
Let me guess: everyone's dead, yours and mine?...
Worse. You had an Order mole sitting in the next building this whole time.
...What?

Fanatic shot his own group in the back. I didn't find him among the bodies. The passage in the tunnel was blown up, you can't get further. Looks like he killed his own and went on, down below. You've been nursing a snake in your bosom...

You know what I thought when you asked about him this morning? "What a Pripyat paranoid, sees traitors everywhere"... Hah, "long enough to trust him with half the group", that's what I said?... Long enough to hand half the group over to him for slaughter, damn it...
You couldn't have known.

I could... I should have! I'm the fucking leader of the group, I'm supposed to sense these things! He... he changed after the trip to Yantar. I thought he'd grown up, but it turns out... Alright, Lieutenant, it doesn't matter anymore. It's time to answer all your questions... I'll start with that case, I guess.
There were artifacts in it?
How did you...?
Horus told me. At first I didn't believe him, but now...

He told you right. Your people confiscate artifacts from our people every day, and by regulations you're supposed to either destroy them or hand them over to the scientists. But, as you can see, your old man was in no hurry to do that. Looks like after what happened at Yantar, shipping artifacts to other mobile bunkers became too expensive and slow, and destroying them... impractical. So Kuznetsov decided to make some money off it, kept such valuable cargo right in your warehouse. He was probably hoping to sell the goods off at a good price someday and set himself up for a comfortable retirement, but something didn't work out...
And he gave that container to you. For a favor?

We're diggers, experts in all kinds of undergrounds, and that's exactly the skill Kuznetsov needed so badly. Why do you think he's kept the garrison here for months and hasn't announced an evacuation with things the way they are? Deep in the underground lies something the Order and the army have been fighting over for months. Maps.
What maps?

Area maps. Down below, on the second level of the underground, there's... an archive, or a stash, hell knows what to call it. It's not just maps: crawlways, trails, passages that aren't on any ordinary maps. The Zone on them is different. The archive's supposedly old, the paper's still Soviet... but all the marks and trails are fresh, literally a month old. And they work.
A true miracle of the Zone. And why does Kuznetsov need them?
I suppose he doesn't want them falling into the Order's hands. Imagine what power the cultists would have if they took the whole archive?
Wait, wait, the whole archive? What do you mean?

The papers were scattered all over P-2, that's what we called the lower level of the Agroprom underground. The Order managed to carry out a small part, but lost too many fighters doing it. Your guys tried too, you saw the result in the tunnel. That's why Kuznetsov turned to us: we'd been down there before and miraculously made it out alive. He paid, we went down and collected as many papers as we could. That container was far from the first, but I hoped it would be the last...
How much did you manage to get out?

Enough. The Order started throwing a wrench in our works way too often, our losses grew, sometimes they managed to intercept our people. But we kept going anyway. Now there's only one stack of maps left in P-2: the last one, but the most important. In short, without it, all the rest is just toilet paper.
Dumb question, but why didn't you get it out right away?
It's at the very end of the underground, as far as I know. Go down to P-2 even once, and you'll understand why we never made it that far.
And now what?
Fanatic and the Order are surely in P-2 right now, looking for a way to the last part of the maps. I won't let him. For once in my whole life I'll go forward, in the front row.
The three of you are going down into the underground? That's suicide.
No, Lieutenant, it's my duty. I've buried four groups with other people's hands, there won't be a fifth. If the Zone wants to take me, let it take me personally.
It was a pleasure doing business with you, Rogovets. An honest soldier in the Zone is a rare thing. Here, take this, my last gift. I took it from one of the wild ones.
Thank you, Seriy.

And one more thing: the moon's bright tonight, but flashlights died with the EMP, and in the shadows or inside buildings you won't see a damn thing. Our shared stash had a few suits with old night-vision goggles, still Soviet. There's barely any electronics in them, they should work even after the EMP. If you want, you can take one. The stash is in the building where Fanatic was staying, in the middle of the anomaly field, under the iron table. Well, this is where our paths part. I don't recommend sticking around here: the Order will surely step up its attacks while the EMP is still in effect. Farewell, soldier.
Farewell, stalker.

Rogovets, this one's for you personally. The guys you pulled out made it back to base. Not all of them, but they made it back. Thank you, Lieutenant, from the bottom of my heart. Drop by the quartermaster, we put together a crate of goodies for you.

Rogovets, this one's for you personally. All three patrols made it back, not a single KIA. Do you even understand what you've done?... If we get out of this, I'll put you up for an award. Drop by the quartermaster, we put together a crate of goodies for you.
Ours... Elite spec ops, they got sent to the most dangerous places. They never made it...
But why didn't the colonel mention this?... Was he hiding it?
And here are the stalkers. I need to examine all of them, figure out what happened.
Entry wound... in the back. This one too. Point-blank, from two meters.
Fourth, fifth... And where's the last one? Where's Fanatic?
All of them shot in the back, I don't see any Order bodies, the passage down is caved in... Fuck, I think I get it...
I need to get back to Seriy, now.
Night already?... How long was I in that tunnel?
%c[fr_radio]Lieutenant... Lieutenant Rogovets, this is the third checkpoint. We need help. Can you hear me? Help us, Lieutenant...
The third... Wait, the radio doesn't work... And the PDA's still dead...
I should check it out anyway. I need to get to the passage to the Garbage.
Two... three... And where are the rest? No signs of a fight, no casings... As if they just got up and left.
So quiet... Too quiet.
%c[fr_chaos]This is the second checkpoint! We're under attack by mutants, requesting help!
No-no-no! That's not the radio. The radio's dead, and I'm not deaf, the first time too...
If there's even one of them alive there, I have to help. Am I a fucking medic or what?!
Ours... In our uniform, with our guns. He led me here on purpose.
...all perso... nnel... ortre... this is Colonel Kuznetsov...

All personnel on the grounds of the Agroprom Research Institute, return to the main base immediately. I repeat: combat alert, everyone to the base immediately, defensive perimeter per plan "Fortress".
Doc... Help me...
Hang in there, soldier. Let me take a look.
[Army medkit and bandage] Hold on, I'll treat it now. This will hurt.
I'm sorry, brother... There's nothing I can do.
Hold on a bit, I'll be right back.
It burns... Everything burns, like my skin was torn off alive...
It's easing up... Thank you. I thought that was it, I was done fighting.
My eyes... Fuuuck, I can't see anything! The fire hit me right in the face...
I can see... Blurry, but I can see! Thank you, brother, I'll never forget it.
The blast threw me off the tower... I can't feel my legs...
Oh... That's better. My legs seem to be there. Thanks, Doc.
I ran to put out the fire, like an idiot... My hands, look what happened to my hands...
Thank you... At least I can hold a rifle again.
Lieutenant Rogovets reporting, Colonel.
Report. What was the shooting by the depot?

Four of them. One was planting a charge under the armory wall, three were keeping watch. The guard at the gate saw them hanging around the fuel tanks before the explosion. I realized right away that the traitors were still on the base, planning their next act of sabotage, and that's what led me to the depot. And they showed up on the PDA... strangely. Their profiles stood out from the overall picture. All the conspirators are dead.
Hm... Of course I'm glad to hear that, Lieutenant... But there are about 40 people on the base right now, are you sure there are no more traitors?
I can't be 100% sure, but I haven't seen any more suspicious soldiers.

I'm not sure either. Well, at least we managed to expose some of them, thanks for that. But just in case, keep your back to the wall, you can expect anything from these scumbags. Alright, enough of that. What about the stalkers?

The camp is gone. People in our uniforms came to them, with your order word for word, and opened fire. Seriy and 2 other stalkers survived, the rest are KIA. He refused to come with me and headed to the lower levels of the Agroprom underground, for the maps.
...So you already know.

I know, Colonel. About the case, about the artifacts, about the archive. About 6 of our men lying down there, in heavy armor. And about you paying for it with confiscated goods you were supposed to destroy by regulations.
Seriy told you?
He did, and... somebody else.

Well, since everybody knows everything... Yes, I was stockpiling. Ever since Yantar fell, I was stockpiling. At first for myself. I thought I'd finish my service, sell it and go somewhere without all this. But then headquarters stopped answering, the supplies ran out, and I realized these artifacts were the only thing I could still use to pay anyone for anything. Those soldiers you saw, they're far from the only ones. Before them I'd already lost 2 groups down there. The best ones, damn it... That's when I realized it's better to pay money for other people's deaths than to lose my own. Especially since Seriy and his stalkers crawl around the undergrounds all the time, they're better at it than we are. And for a while they really did manage to bring us parts of the maps. Not all of them, I'll be honest, but better than nothing.
Why didn't you tell anyone what was really going on?

What for? The men were already on edge, and this way they'd have started deserting outright... Well, why are you looking at me like that? Go on, judge me, tell me how wrong I am, and blah-blah-blah...
I won't.
...And why's that?
Because at least you were paying for something. Others would just send soldiers to an endless slaughter without a second thought. In our situation there was no other choice.

That's right, Lieutenant. Thanks for understanding... Alright, enough of that. Let's get to the plan. What do we have right now? No contact with the Big Land for two days, no fuel, a little over 40 combat-ready men, basically no vehicles, the enemy has us completely surrounded, visibility close to zero... Lousy, don't you think? Was it like this for you guys in Pripyat?
Even worse, it was a branch of hell on Earth. And back then we had no hope, but here...

Right, Rogovets. The only thing we have left lies down below. If the Order takes the last part of the maps, everything we've been dying for these past weeks was for nothing. We need that last part no matter what... That's why you're going down there.
I... I'm starting to get used to it, Colonel.

You've been walking the surface all day, carrying out the most dangerous assignments and surviving where whole squads died. I wasn't wrong about you after all... Don't worry, you won't go alone, our underground garrison will go with you. I tried to contact the sergeant, but no fucking luck, there's no signal underground. So you'll tell him about the mission in person. Drop by the quartermaster one last time, he'll give you our best gear... Lieutenant Rogovets, are you ready to carry out the mission?
Yes, sir!
Get to it. In the meantime I'll organize the defense, the cultists clearly won't keep us waiting long and will show up here soon. Good luck, soldier.
Hello, I'm here for...

Yeah, the colonel already told me. Here, take it. The last spec ops combat kit, we were saving it for a rainy day. It's got the newest night vision built in, it shouldn't have been hit by the EMP. And a Groza on top of that. Not much ammo, though, so sorry about that. Worst case, smash 'em in the face with the stock, heh-heh.
Thanks. As I recall, this morning you said you didn't have any armor except torn rags?...
Hah, you didn't forget. And what was I supposed to do, just hand over our last set of armor to you, a wimpy medic? Or mention it and then tell you to fuck off?
Fair enough.

That's what I'm saying. That's it, go on, don't hang around here, you've got a mission. And I think I'll hand out the remaining ammo and head to the barricades. Oh, it's been a long time since I picked up a saber...
Medic, finally!
Report, soldier, what happened here?
Somebody blew up the fuel depot! These guys were nearby, wounded. Two more KIA, they're still lying over there...
Damn it... What about these guys? What's their condition?
Uh, I don't know, I'm not a medic! They're in really bad shape, critical, probably. And I've got no meds at all...
I had some. Step aside.
I helped whoever I could.
Uh-huh. Too bad not everyone. Well, thanks anyway, Doc. Here, take this.
You've got hands of gold, brother! Thank you so much! Here, take this.
It's my duty. Tell me about the explosion in detail.
I was on duty at the main entrance. Couldn't see a fucking thing: pitch-black darkness, and on top of that all the electronics died, they only just came back. I didn't notice any outsiders, but...
But...?
Fuck, I just don't believe it! It can't be...
Talk, soldier.

Ahem... Basically, out of the corner of my eye I saw a couple of our guys hanging around the fuel tanks. I didn't look closely at what exactly they were doing, I just saw them nearby. They hung around there for about 5 minutes, then left, and 5 minutes later, the explosion... I just imagined it, right? We don't have any traitors... We're all... comrades, right?
If only that were true. Get some rest, soldier, there's a hard night ahead.
Sergeant, wake up!
Lieutenant?... You... hah... You again. Who else, of course...
Quiet, don't waste your breath. Let me look... Shrapnel. Fuck... the lung is hit.

I figured that out without you... Fu-u-uck... It hurts so bad... My own guys did this to me... Those idiots threw a grenade... in an enclosed, goddamn, space. I told them... told them not to throw them... only made it worse... morons...
[Scientific medkit] Alright, lie still, don't move. This will hurt, but you'll live. Hold on.
Argh... fuck... You...
Breathe. That's it. Better now?
Better... You're a goddamn wizard... Wait, what the hell are you even doing here?
The colonel's orders. I was supposed to take your squad and go down to P-2, for the maps. Not meant to be, from the looks of it.
What about my guys?!
I saved who I could, but the losses are heavy. Gather all the survivors and go back to the base, Sergeant, there's nothing for you down there.
Yeah, yeah... Just let me catch my breath a bit...
Tell me, what happened here?

Can't you see for yourself? An attack and a total rout... Lieutenant, they... They didn't come, they were always here. It's like they came out of the ground... And some of ours turned out to be traitors too... Opened fire on us from behind without a second thought. Scumbags, just animals... Who are they, Rogovets?!
Long story. All you need to know: if you see people with "eyes" on their suits, shoot to kill.

I figured that much out after what happened... Listen, you need to go down, right? So listen: when all this started, I saw some stalkers walk past us, right through the fight. Three of them. Not shooting, not hiding, they just walked past. One in front, so calm, and then down below. I marked it on your PDA.
Seriy... So he made it. I'll go after him. Don't stay here, head straight upstairs. And blow up the damn passage behind you.
And what about you?!
I'll find another way, I'm sure there is one. The main thing is, don't let these bastards get behind us.
I... I've got nothing, I'm sorry. I can't pull you through with a regular medkit, Sergeant. The shrapnel's in your lung, you...
I get it, Doc, I'm not new here. Don't be sad. At least somebody was honest with me today... Rogovets... Take care of my guys...
I'll do everything I can. Goodbye.
Private Skriptovich
Fuck! That's the fuel depot... Our fuel is fucked. I hope nobody got hurt...
Medic, goddammit, where the hell are you?! Get to the infirmary ON THE DOUBLE, I've got half a squad here with burns!
Rogovets, what's all that shooting in the yard?!
Taking out the trash. We've got traitors on the base.
Hm.... Come up to my office.
SOS, SOS, we're under attack! They're coming from all sides, we need help!
Where are they coming from... Hey, soldier, I'm on your side, don't shoot!
I'm hit, goddammit...
Pitch black... And so quiet I can hear my heart beating.
Ours... They've been lying here a long time. Must be those two groups the colonel talked about.
Seriy's guys, those two from the camp... So he's somewhere nearby too.
Seriy... He made it after all, all the way to the end. He just couldn't get out. The maps should be on him. So many people died for these papers...
%c[fr_chaos]Kill them all, every last one!
Footsteps behind me... Heavy ones. Someone's coming.
It's started... The base, the colonel, the guys... I have to get upstairs, fast!
Fuck, I'm hit... Goddamn sniper...
I won't... I won't let them have the maps...
A former stalker from Seriy's group. Gunned down his own in the tunnel and went over to the Order.
Zombies, coming from all sides! Everyone who can, to the main entrance, move!
Rogovets, you alive? Did you find it?!
Found it, Colonel. I've got everything.
Excellent!! If we survive, I'll put you up for an award. Listen: the guys are trying to fix the chopper. There's enough fuel in the tank for one flight, if they get the engine started.
We have to hold out as long as we can, we need to buy our technicians more time. Defensive positions, men!
North entrance, the enemy's breaking through!... Jesus fucking Christ, what the hell are those?!
They're blowing up the walls, enemy in the rear!
Traitors on the base, I repeat, traitors on...
I see the Order's main force, coming from the northeast. Opening fire...
Fuck, our sniper's down! Rogovets, get up on the roof, you're taking his place!
RPG!!! TAKE COVER!!
Fucking hell... Our evac is screwed... Malevich! You there?!
Here... still alive.
The chopper's fucked, we're not getting out by air. Go up to my office and take all the maps from my desk, THAT'S AN ORDER!
Yes, sir!
What've you got, Sergeant?
Got the documents, coming do... Son of a... Snipers on the hill...
Fuck, Sergeant! Rogovets, take out the snipers and get the documents from the sergeant!
I've got the maps, Colonel!
Listen to me carefully, soldier... We won't win this fight... We've got 80% casualties, lots of KIA... I'm wounded myself... I order you to drop everything and fall back immediately...
Negative! I won't leave you all here.
Wake up, Lieutenant! There are over a hundred of them, and there's maybe 15 of us left at best. The Order's main force is advancing, all of them in heavy armor, with machine guns...
Colonel, sir...
As you were! Rogovets, the most important thing right now is the maps. That's what dozens of good men died for, and if they fall into the hands of these... scumbags... Then it was all for nothing.
You can jump over the south wall... Get out that way. I marked a safe route on your PDA. Head for the hatch... There's an underground tunnel there, it'll take you to the Cordon...
Remember, Lieutenant, the maps MUST NOT fall into their hands. It's the only thing that made any sense today... And me... I'm going into my last fight...
MEN, LET'S CLEAR THE WAY FOR THE LIEUTENANT. OPEN FIRE ON THE ENEMY WITH EVERYTHING WE'VE GOT!
Doc, this is the infirmary duty officer! The guys you patched up are back in the fight, we're holding the infirmary. Thank you, brother!
Doc, it's the duty officer! The ones you pulled through are armed again. Not all of them, of course... But we're holding!
Doc... It's the duty officer. I'm holding the infirmary alone. None of the ones they brought in made it...
Lieutenant, it's the sergeant from the underground! We came up and blew the passage, like you said. Almost all the guys are with me, we're holding our sector!
Lieutenant, it's the sergeant from the underground! We came up, blew the passage. Only a couple of men with me... But we're holding!
Lieutenant, this is the underground garrison! The sergeant's gone... We blew the passage behind us so these bastards can't hit us from behind. We're holding our sector!
Lieutenant... There's only two of us left from the underground. The sergeant's dead. We blew the passage... There's nobody else.
Thanks for your help, stalker! If you hadn't shown up, I'd be a dead man by now.
I am looking for information about Strelok, maybe you know something?
How do I get into the basement?
Strelok's secret stash?
Thanks for the information.
Yes, I heard about that. They even say he used to "work" in these parts and Strelok's stash is in the local basements. Rumor has it that his group's base was here too.
This is one of the many exits which will lead you into the interconnected basements. Once you're in there, you're on your own - I don't have a map and the basement network is huge and confusing.
I'm looking for info on Strelok. Seriy told me you know something about him.
Thank you.
Yeah, we looked for it too but couldn't find it. I'll send you some info about it. That's everything we have on the stash.
What's going on here?
We're fighting, or more specifically, camping out like sitting ducks. Talk to Mole if you want to know more - he's the leader.
Man, that was a fight and a half - you wouldn't wish something like that on your worst enemy. Those army boys are getting pretty cocky!
Where is the Agroprom Research Institute?
Not far from here. Follow the road to the West and you'll come to the Institute's gates.
I hear the military have set up a base there, right?
Thanks for the information.

Yeah, there's a military base. I'm not sure how many of them there are exactly but it's at least a platoon. They're well-armed and you've got no chance of breaking through - they'll take you down before you can say "hello, comrades". The best way of getting in is during the night 'cause the base is well-guarded during the day - they got checkpoints everywhere and anyway, I heard a deserter-soldier from that base is hiding in the marshes. If you can find him I'm sure you can shake some useful info out of him.
What's going on?
Me and my boys found a nice little area full of artifacts but those army bastards attacked us for some reason. I don't know what the hell they wanted from us...

Yeah, I've heard about him. I think he used to "make his living" in this area - it's quite a good place, actually. He left a long time ago; I don't know when it was exactly and I've got no clue where he was headed. That's everything I can tell you.
You weren't waiting here for no reason, were you? Otherwise why would the Spetsnaz show up here?
OK, I know something about Strelok.
Yeah? I really need to know that!
If you lied to me, I'll find you and finish what the soldiers couldn't!
I'm not lying. I know that nobody trusts anyone here so you have little choice.

Seriy? Well, OK, listen. They say Strelok used to sneak around here. On top of that, his stash is somewhere around here below ground. I heard his group even has its base here. We also looked for the stash but we found jack shit. I'll give you the info about the stash, maybe you'll be luckier. This is everything we have on the stash.
What else do you know?
I don't know anything else. I told you everything I knew and now you have to work it out on your own. Good luck to you.
Help me, stalker!!!
OK.
Don't shoot, man!
What are you doing?

I'm coming back from the factory which is a bit further down the road. I don't know how but the army found out about our group. I didn't wait for them to show up and took off as quickly as I could. I hope our boys got out of there 'cause otherwise they won't be alive for much longer - you saw the choppers yourself.
I see, thanks.
I see, thanks.
I've got a couple of questions.
What do you want to know?
Anything interesting in the area?
How much do you need?
Here, take the money. Now tell me where it is.
Piss off!
Thank you.
Yeah, there are a couple of places but you'll have to share some of your wealth, buddy.
It used to be pretty quiet but now the army has got all excited and started wasting everyone. They smoked the bandits out recently and I hear some managed to escape into the catacombs.
Thirty, deal?

The exit from the railway tunnel is nearby. It's fairly safe in the dead end. At least nobody has been eaten while sleeping...yet. Also, to the Northwest of the factory you'll find a marsh with a wagon in it. But be careful, there's a shitload of radiation around it, so it's best to approach it from the western side. Oh, and one more thing: a soldier has been spotted there. He's likely to be from the military base at the Institute. The poor bastard is probably crazy - he's been there for a couple of days and I doubt he'll survive much longer on his own.
Bye!
Anything interesting happening here?
Do you know about Ratcatcher? The info will cost you 30.
Deal.
We have a local hero around here called Ratcatcher. He lives in the marshes. The man bred so many rats in the collectors that they'll soon eat those army bastards.
Great. Thanks.
Tell me more about the collectors.
Collectors are your standard shit-stinking sewers that take waste from the Institute and dumps it in the nearest water reservoir.
Great. See you and take care of yourself.
I know that already. Thanks.
I don't have anything else to tell you.
I don't have enough cash.
I'm not interested.
Anything interesting happening here?
Nothing. Absolutely nothing.
I see. Bye!
Tell me about this place.

This is the area around the Agroprom Research Institute. The Institute itself is to the Southwest. The factory, which served as the Institute's technical production facility, is to the North. The buildings have been abandoned for a long time and there's nothing to be found there, but the army has been searching there very actively recently.
Tell me more about the Institute.

There are loads of legends about the Institute. Before the accident in 1986 the only thing here was the Institute of Crop Selection and Genetics. The area where the factory is now was used for experimental crop fields. After the accident, they closed the Institute and burned the fields. Then they remembered about it, they whitewashes the building, put up a fence around it and built some barracks. I don't know what they did at the Institute but they didn't have any shortage of funding, that's for sure.
Tell me more about the factory.

The factory was built at the end of the 80s. They said it was going to be used to build and test machines that could treat soil affected by radiation. As far as I know, nobody ever saw a single machine come out of that plant. It's totally empty now, which makes it a favorite spot for stalkers. I hear the place is pretty safe as long as you avoid the dark corners.
Thank you.
What are you doing?
I'm hiding here, I don't want no trouble.
Who are you hiding from?
Catacombs?
Do you know where they keep documents at the Institute?
What are you going to do now?
What are you going to do now?

I am from the recon unit. They sent us into the catacombs to see what's going on below the base. It's hell down there, I'm telling you. I was the only one to get out of there... everyone else is probably dead by now. I don't want to go back to the base - those bastards are always using us to plug up all the holes in this damn Zone.
Underground tunnels. They go from the Institute to the area around it - I'll show you the entrances. I don't have maps of the catacombs themselves.

At the HQ. It's on the third floor of the Institute. That's where they keep those damn papers. But it's a mission getting there. By day, the area is teaming with patrols but not as much at night. I'll tell you this for free: if you wanna get inside you'll have to go through the catacombs - you stand no chance at the gate.

Hmm. I don't know. I am a deserter according to the military code and I need to get out of the Zone somehow. When we first got here there was a Zaporozhets in the garage that was almost working. I brought it back to life in half an hour but that damn captain took it for himself claiming he should have it according to the code. He drove it along this road and dumped it in the rain by the gate. If only I could get that car - making a run for it is much safer on wheels!
Hello.
What's up?
Tell me about the collector. How do I get inside? Where are the exits and entrances?

It's dangerous inside the collector. There are six entrances and two of them are in the area around the Institute where the military have set up a base. That area is patrolled and the captain keeps the patrol schedule in his armory.
How do you know all that?
The rats told me.
I see. Bye! Good luck to you.
Nothing. See you.
Who are you?
I live here, if you can call this a life. I breed rats in the collector to annoy the military at the Institute.
I am Ratcatcher.
What are you doing in this marsh?
Oh... I get it.... well, I'm from another story. Ha-ha-ha...
